title: Slice activation spectra and contingency notes (working)
content:
Purpose:
Small working doc to capture a different framing for staged experiment activation and rapid contingency planning: we call it an activation SPECTRA (a continuum, not just discrete canary buckets). Aim: give cross-functional stewards a compact mental model + checklist for running interleaved canaries / ABs where cost, latency and safety can pull in different directions.

Scope:
- Applies to product router launches, LLM-based features where we have multiple model variants + routing policies.
- Focused on 3 things: 1) how we partition slices (cohorts) along a spectrum of exposure intensity, 2) clear escalation & fallback paths per-slice, 3) minimal telemetry + sentinel signals for rapid decisioning.

Key definitions (working):
- Spectrum of activation (SPECTRA): a linear framing from SMOKE -> MICRO -> PULSE -> RAMP -> FULL. Each step increases exposure and blast radius.
- Slice: a group of traffic defined by behavior, geography, device, or product persona.
- Steward: named human (or role) responsible for observation/decisioning for a slice during activation window.
- Safety corridor: set of signal thresholds that prevent the spectrum from advancing.

SPECTRA tiers (practical notes):
- SMOKE (~0.01%): Synthetic + seeded queries only. Used to validate static instrumentation, routing and immediate failures. No user-facing exposure.
- MICRO (~0.1%): Real user baseline cohort; narrow persona (e.g., internal-beta users, power-users). Short window (15–30m). Focus: correctness, early latency regressions.
- PULSE (~1%): Small live cohort with human-facing metric guardrails (NPS-ish signals optional). Monitor for quality drift, hallucination spikes.
- RAMP (5–20%): Broader geo/persona coverage. Run extended telemetry for 24–72h, include cost telemetry to check unit economics.
- FULL (100%): Release if all safety corridors held and business KPIs look reasonable.

Slice taxonomy suggestions (choose 3–5 for any launch):
- Persona (new user / returning / power-user)
- Intent (transactional vs exploratory)
- Device type + region (mobile EU / desktop NA)
- Error history / recency (users that hit 50% error last 7d)
Notes: prefer orthogonal slices to minimize overlap. We should maintain a lightweight invertible index so we can reconstruct overlaps quickly.

Ownership & stewarding ritual (proposal):
- Each activation has a named steward per slice: steward + backup + oncall pager contact.
- Steward duties: 1) confirm smoke checks, 2) monitor signal dashboard until 2 consecutive windows are green, 3) advance spectrum or trigger contingency runbook.
- Pre-launch: short async sign-off in Slack channel with timestamped artifact (PR link + config checksum).

Minimum observable signal set (MOSS): (these are the absolute minimum to progress between SPECTRA tiers)
- Latency p50/p95/p99 by slice and model variant (trend + absolute)
- Error rate (5xx, model failure modes) by slice
- Token cost per request (for generation features) and estimated projected spend at RAMP
- Quality sentinels: rerank hit-rate, hallucination proxy (keyword-based), human-review flags count
- Business KPIs: conversion rate or task success closely tied to feature
- Circuit breakers: throttling events, quota exhaustion events
Notes: each signal requires baseline expectations and a guard (absolute and delta). E.g., p95 must not exceed baseline+200ms OR increase >30% over 1h.

Contingency categories & quick actions (decision ladder):
- Soft-degradation (quality dip but healthy infra): scale back SPECTRA one step (e.g., from RAMP -> PULSE), increase sampling for human review, enable model fallback variant.
- Latency/cost spike: divert heavy tails to cheaper variant (routing policy), enable per-tenant cap, throttle noncritical routes.
- Safety violation (hallucination / compliance): immediate freeze (stop advance), for high-severity auto-revert to previous model, initiate incident handler and notify legal/CS if PII exposure.
- Service failure: automated failover per-region, re-route to global stable pool; steward triggers postmortem-runbook.

Concrete fallback primitives (ops knobs):
- Model fallback mapping (variant A -> variant B) with compatibility map (tokenization + schema check)
- Traffic shaping: percent-rollbacks vs absolute-slice-exclusion (e.g., remove small cohorts until stable)
- Greylist: keep requests but instrument responses with headers so we can scrub + revert asynchronously
- Synthetic surge switch: replay recorded flows into sandbox to validate fixes before advancing again

Activation checklist (pre-launch quick run):
- [ ] Config checksum recorded + PR with rollout config link
- [ ] Steward + backup listed in activation slack thread and document
- [ ] Smoke synthetic suite mapped and green (include sample seed set)
- [ ] MOSS dashboard screens configured and pinned to steward watches
- [ ] Pre-bake fallback mappings in router (policy id) and validate with dry-run
- [ ] Cost projection calc for RAMP, sign-off from finance if >$X/day
- [ ] Human-review queue & threshold set (sampling rate, escalation path)

Escalation scripts (short phrases to use in slack + pages):
- "SMOKE FAIL: routing 5xx — rolling back to stable-2025-07-31, steward @sofia-nguyen oncall"
- "PULSE QUALITY ALERT: halluc proxy > threshold (3x) — freeze advance, enabling fallback-embeddings-v2"
- "RAMP LATENCY: p95 increased 40% — throttle explore routes to 20% and reassign slices"

Simulation & rehearsal ideas (low effort):
- Micro-surge test: artificially inject 2–3x traffic to a PULSE cohort using synthetic generator for 10m to validate autoscale & backpressure
- Obfuscated-hallucination test: seed templates that historically trigger model hallucinations and ensure SLA for human-review path works
- Interleaved AB stress: run two competing rollouts with non-overlapping slices to measure interference on shared infra/kvcache

Data & instrumentation notes (practical):
- Prefer event-first logging (one line per request) with tags: slice_id, steward, model_variant, routing_policy. Keep schema stable.
- Keep a small daily derived table for overlap heatmaps (slice vs slice) to estimate collision risk when multiple activations run concurrently.
- Backfill policy: if we detect correlated drift across slices, capture raw inputs for 72h only under access control for eval.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How rigid should SPECTRA thresholds be? (absolute vs relative). Suggestation: baseline for infra signals, relative for quality. Need team decision. (ACTION: product + infra sync)
- Ownership for overlap heatmap: infra telemetry or product analytics? (ACTION: assign by EOW)
- Auto-rollback gating: which signals can trigger automated rollback vs require human ack? Proposal: infra failures => auto; quality/safety => require steward confirm.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Ethan: prototype MOSS dashboard template (due 2025-06-25)
- Mariana: draft config-checksum tool spec + implement small cli to snapshot rollout configs (due 2025-07-03)
- Sofia: run two rehearsals (micro-surge + interleaved AB) in staging and document findings (due 2025-07-10)

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Want this to be light: teams dislike big rigid SOPs. SPECTRA framing helps teams think in terms of intensity not only percent.
- Consider adding a small per-experiment metadata blob: {steward, spectrum-start, token-cost-estimate} — keep it minimal to support automations.
- Link to related artifacts: CONFLUENCE-1234 (rollout lexicon), JIRA-RD-INF-867 (router fallback feature branch).

End of working notes.

Quick links and references:
- Slack channel: #rollout-orchestra 
- Incident playbook: CONFLUENCE-INCIDENTS-2
- Router policy docs: https://internal.redwood/docs/router-policies
